new_entities.name: Therapeutic ketogenic diet
new_entities.description: A carbohydrate-restricted diet designed to induce sustained nutritional ketosis for therapeutic purposes.

new_entities.name: Bipolar mood stabilization
aliases: improved mood stability in bipolar disorder
new_entities.description: Stabilization of depressive, hypomanic, or manic symptom burden in bipolar disorder.

edges.effect_quant: The best trial-like bipolar data are still pilot and observational. In the 2025 Edinburgh pilot, standard mood scales in euthymic bipolar participants did not change significantly over 6 to 8 weeks, even though higher ketone levels tracked with better daily self-rated mood and energy.
edges.population: adults with bipolar disorder participating in pilot ketogenic interventions or metabolic-therapy case studies
edges.mechanism: A ketogenic diet may affect bipolar symptoms through altered brain energy metabolism, glutamate-GABA balance, mitochondrial efficiency, and ion-channel signaling. But those theoretical benefits compete with strong selection effects, adherence challenges, and the possibility that metabolic change improves energy or anxiety without producing robust syndromal stabilization.
edges.summary: The bipolar ketogenic literature is promising but far from settled. Pilot and case-based reports suggest some people experience better day-to-day mood stability, yet the only structured pilot data so far are small and do not show a clean randomized-style efficacy signal on standard bipolar mood scales.
edges.caveats: Most available evidence is open-label, pilot, or case-based, and some cohorts were euthymic at baseline, which limits room for improvement. This edge should be treated as experimental metabolic psychiatry rather than established bipolar maintenance therapy.

evidence.notes: A pilot study of a ketogenic diet in bipolar disorder: clinical, metabolic and magnetic resonance spectroscopy findings.
